pr_title: Limit rainbird aiohttp client session to a single connection
pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Limit rainbird aiohttp client session to a single connection so that any concurrent requests are queued rather than issued in parallel. This should fix any issues with rainbird stability due to concurrent requests either from the data coordinator, UI, or automations.

Manually tested:
- Without this change: If you spam the sprinkler switch on and off over and over again it will fail with an error due to the device being busy
- With the change:  If you spam the sprinkler switch on and off over and over again it always succeeds.

Additionally manually tested config flows, adding and removing/disabling the config entries, etc and verifying all connections are closed properly.

issue_context.title: Rainbird integration is loosing connection when switches are used in automation
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I played around with automating my rainbird irrigation system with home assistant. I noticed a weird behaviour.
When using the sprinkler switches manually with the UI, i did not notice any issues.

But when using sprinkler switches in an automation, the rainbird integrations throws an error when sprinkler is turned off => rainbird device is busy. He is indeed turning off the sprinkler, but then not reacting for about 1-2 minutes.

Logs showing this:
Logger: homeassistant.components.rainbird.coordinator
Source: helpers/update_coordinator.py:345
Integration: Rain Bird (documentation, issues)
First occurred: 27. Februar 2024 um 19:27:58 (2 occurrences)
Last logged: 27. Februar 2024 um 19:31:55

Error fetching 192.168.xx.xx (ips xxxed) data: Rain Bird device is busy
![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/68947111/60874ec4-b973-4808-8bd9-acbc8d67bd07)

![image](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/assets/68947111/5d794b96-3d49-46b6-8f5d-f7de4459f27c)



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2024.2.3

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

rainbird

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rainbird/

### Diagnostics information

### Example YAML snippet


The rainbird device has a limitation where it can only accept one command at a time.  The rainbird client library does try to do some backoff and wait to be resiliant to these problems, however sending more requests can just make it worse so we try to not hammer the device with retries.

I wonder if part of the problem here is a synchronization between the rainbird device polling and the automation.  e.g. say home assistant is polling the device (every minute) around the same time as the automation is running (exactly one minute away).  I noticed the error message fetching the device data are around the same time as the automation error message.

I'm trying to think about a real solution here, but in the mean time i wonder if having a slight adjustment on the delay results in a different outcome...

Wouldn't it help to add a `asyncio.Lock()` in the rainbird coordinator code so that a poll and an update are not done in parallel? The daikin_onecta integration on which I recently did a lot of work also uses that, see https://github.com/jwillemsen/daikin_onecta/blob/7c1811a247c26eeb27078d60e47088c419c92830/custom_components/daikin_onecta/daikin_api.py#L51

Following this issue because I see the same when I use an automation to set the rain delay when a separate rain sensor has detected a lot of rain during the day

Great suggestion, it may help. We sometimes see that it can handle requests that arrive at the sametime other times it can't or rejects them even when not arriving at the same time with each other.  I think it would be useful to see a debug log trace as the client library can show is in more details what requests were being issued.

review_comments: Probably close the session on Home Assistant stop too.

I considered this, but intentionally left this out because it seemed like a lot of code with unclear benefit to me. I think it makes sense for a connection pool with thousands of connections, but for a single connection it seemed fine to just wait for unload? I've sent PR #112292 however since you've asked for it.
What do you mean "to just wait for unload"?
